name: hydrothermal_carbon_fixation
description: A reusable H2/pH-driven carbon-fixation module. Module C = genuine FiPy Nernst-Planck pH-gradient electrochemistry (pmf, current density). Module D = genuine eQuilibrator ΔG' feasibility gate + lab-calibrated (Preiner/Hudson) mineral-catalyzed CO2 reduction to formate/acetate/pyruvate. gradient_efficiency=1.0 is the favorable arm; ~0.1 is the Tutolo-2026 in-situ collapse. catalyst_active/h2=0 give the controls. Requires equilibrator_api + fipy.

gradient_efficiency.description: Usable fraction of the geochemical ΔpH at in-situ T/P (1.0 favorable; ~0.1 Tutolo-2026 collapse; 0 = no-gradient control)

catalyst_active.description: Active Fe/Ni/S mineral catalyst (0 = no-catalyst control)

dilution_rate.description: Open-flow washout (1/s); 0 = closed batch (yield studies), >0 = open vent reactor → sustained-throughput regime (phase map)

gradient.doc:
Real 1-D FiPy electroneutral Nernst-Planck proton electrodiffusion across
the Fe(Ni)S barrier. Reads the vent (alkaline) and ocean (acidic) pH plus
temperature, solves the steady proton profile with the genuine FiPy FVM
solver, and emits the usable ΔpH, proton-motive force, diffusion potential
and current density (bare-float deltas toward the transported steady value;
overwrite sensors for the conservation witness).

_contract.summary: Real 1-D FiPy electroneutral Nernst-Planck proton electrodiffusion across the Fe(Ni)S barrier.
_contract.description: Reads the vent (alkaline) and ocean (acidic) pH plus temperature, solves the steady electroneutral proton profile with the genuine FiPy finite-volume solver, and emits the usable delta-pH, proton-motive force, diffusion potential and current density as overwrite sensors (the current state of the barrier, not an accumulating pool), with the FVM balance residual as a conservation witness. gradient_efficiency scales the favorable (1.0) vs the Tutolo-2026 in-situ (~0.1) proton-gradient arm.

outputs.delta_pH: usable proton gradient across the barrier (dimensionless)

assumptions: Steady electroneutral Nernst-Planck profile each step (fast relative to the vent).

budget.doc:
Conserved proton reservoir coupling the pH-gradient source to carbon
fixation with chemiosmotic back-pressure.

Reads the open-circuit proton-motive force (what the geochemical ΔpH could
supply) and the carbon-fixation flux (the load), integrates the proton
reservoir under geochemical supply − stoichiometric draw − leak, and emits
the **loaded** pmf (sagging with state of charge) plus the budget sensors.
All outputs are overwrite sensors — the current state of the proton economy,
not accumulating pools (the reservoir itself is integrated internally).

_contract.summary: Conserved proton budget: the pH gradient is a finite reservoir that carbon fixation spends, with the loaded pmf sagging under load (chemiosmotic back-pressure).
_contract.description: Integrates a proton reservoir d(R)/dt = supply - protons_per_carbon * carbon_flux - leak * R (capped at capacity), and outputs the LOADED proton-motive force pmf_loaded = pmf_open * (R / capacity). Carbon fixation reads pmf_loaded, so drawing the reservoir down throttles fixation (respiratory-control back-pressure); the system settles at a loaded steady state with pmf_loaded < pmf_open while carbon is fixed, and relaxes toward open-circuit as the load falls. Remove supply and both collapse. All outputs are overwrite sensors; the reservoir is integrated internally.

inputs.pmf_open: open-circuit proton-motive force from the geochemical gradient (volt)
inputs.carbon_flux: net organic-carbon fixation rate — the load (mole/second)

outputs.pmf: loaded (back-pressured) proton-motive force fixation actually sees (volt)
outputs.proton_draw: protons spent by fixation this instant = protons_per_carbon * carbon_flux (mole/second)
outputs.proton_supply: protons delivered by the geochemical gradient (mole/second)

math: dR/dt = supply - protons_per_carbon * carbon_flux - leak * R
assumptions: protons_per_carbon H+ translocated down the gradient per carbon fixed (Wood-Ljungdahl/Rnf-Ech bioenergetic stoichiometry).
Steady geochemical proton supply from serpentinization; first-order passive leak.

thermo.doc:
Real eQuilibrator feasibility gate: ``(pH, I, T, H2, CO2, products) ->
ΔG' + feasibility`` for formate/acetate/pyruvate synthesis.

A ``Step`` (stateless per tick; it reads conditions and emits sensor
readings). The ComponentContribution engine + the per-reaction ΔG'° are
cached (ΔG'° recomputed only when pH/I/T change) so it is cheap to run every
tick.

_contract.summary: Real eQuilibrator feasibility gate: (pH, I, T, H2, CO2, products) -> dG' + feasibility for formate/acetate/pyruvate synthesis.
_contract.description: A stateless Step: each tick it reads the vent conditions and emits the real eQuilibrator physiological dG' (ComponentContribution, offline) for H2-driven CO2 reduction to formate / acetate / pyruvate, plus a feasibility multiplier in [0,1] (logistic in -dG'/RT) that gates the downstream kinetics. dG'0 is cached and recomputed only when pH / ionic strength / temperature change.

outputs.free_energy_logged: witness that dG' was logged this tick (dimensionless)

assumptions: Physiological (transformed) dG' at the given pH / I / T.

fixation.doc:
Lab-calibrated mineral-catalyzed CO2 reduction, gated by thermodynamic
feasibility, proton-motive drive, substrate availability and catalyst.

Emits product concentration increments (bare ``float`` deltas — pools
accumulate) and the net organic-carbon flux (overwrite sensor).

_contract.summary: Lab-calibrated mineral-catalyzed CO2 reduction, gated by thermodynamic feasibility, proton drive, availability and catalyst.
_contract.description: Emits product concentration increments (additive float deltas - pools accumulate) for H2-driven CO2 reduction to formate / acetate / pyruvate on Fe/Ni/S mineral catalysts, with the rate gated by the eQuilibrator feasibility, the proton-motive drive, substrate availability (H2, CO2), a temperature window and headroom to the Preiner-calibrated yield caps. Net organic-carbon flux is an overwrite sensor.

inputs.catalyst_activity: active Fe/Ni/S catalyst in [0,1] (dimensionless; 0 = no-mineral control)

assumptions: Yields capped at Preiner/Hudson lab values (formate 0.2 M, acetate 1e-4, pyruvate 1e-5).
rate = k * catalyst * feasible * drive(pmf) * avail(H2,CO2) * T-window * headroom.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
